title: Lighthouse onboarding mosaic: visual system for Quickstart landing
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Create a cohesive visual system for the Quickstart landing page that communicates onboarding flow at a glance. Deliver a hero snapshot, three contextual step diagrams, and two responsive screenshot treatments for web and mobile. Emphasis on developer clarity, scannability, and brand-forward illustrative motifs.
background: Current quickstart landing visuals are inconsistent across docs and marketing. Users report confusion about which Quickstart path to take (API, Dedicated, Private). We want a single visual approach that scales to product variants and is easy for engineers to swap into docs and SDK guides.
goals: Reduce first-time user dropoff on Quickstart landing by improving comprehension of available paths
Ship a reusable set of hero and step visuals that can be mirrored across docs, onboarding modals, and release landing pages
Provide production-ready artboards and annotated specs for engineering to implement responsive assets
deliverables: Hero mosaic artwork (SVG + PNG export): developer-focused scene showing 'Start - Integrate - Deploy' lanes
Three step diagrams: API Quickstart, Dedicated onboarding, Private deployment overview (each 3-panel microflow)
Two screenshot treatments: desktop code+console composite and vertical mobile stack for guides
Annotated specs: spacing, color tokens, accessibility contrast notes, responsive breakpoints
Variant set: light/dark theme and high-contrast token versions
out_of_scope: Copy rewrite beyond short hero headline and microcopy for step labels
Building frontend components or integrating assets into the live site (handled by ENG)
acceptance_criteria: All artboards provided in SVG and optimized PNG with transparent and flat backgrounds
Design tokens and spacing documented as copy-paste-ready in the handoff spec
Assets reviewed and approved by PM and Brand (approval comment in ticket)
Screenshot treatments validated against live console data and device sizes: 1366x768, 1440x900, 375x812
Accessibility checks: hero contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary CTA copy; step labels >= 3:1 for body text
tasks: Discovery: audit existing quickstart visuals and capture inconsistencies (Marina)
Iterate concept A into hero mosaic and step microflows (Jonah)
Create responsive screenshot templates and capture console snapshots (Design Ops)
Compile handoff package and add tokens + export presets (Marina)
Design review with PM + Brand + Engineering, collect feedback (All)
Finalize exports, push to shared Drive, update docs reference links (Jonah)
design_decisions: Use a horizontal mosaic hero that visualizes three canonical paths rather than a single hero image to reduce ambiguity
Prefer simplified isometric motifs and line-weights that reproduce well at small sizes for step diagrams
Keep color palette aligned with product tokens; introduce single accent hue for callouts to avoid vibrancy clashes
Avoid heavy literal metaphors (e.g., servers as mountains) in favor of developer tooling metaphors (terminal, waveform, cluster tiles)
tradeoffs_considered: More detailed illustrations would increase clarity but add weight and slow page loads; chosen compromise: SVG with simplified fills and PNG fallbacks
Animating the hero could draw attention but requires engineering effort and accessibility controls; deferred to a follow-up ticket
One-off hero per product variant vs single combined hero: combined hero reduces duplication but may obscure unique onboarding nuances; decided to create combined hero with small variant badges
review_feedback: PM Riya: prefer stronger headline hierarchy; suggested reducing hero subcopy to one line
Brand Asha: request to soften secondary accent color and align stroke thickness with icon set
Engineering Tomas: asked for separate exports for retina and non-retina and explicit padding values for CSS implementation
Docs Lucas: requested example callouts that link to 'Start API Quickstart' and 'Request Dedicated Trial' anchors
